conviction_note: The event is real: Fabasoft pre-announced its H1 2026/27 report for 2026-11-13, and its last two releases went out at 07:17 and 07:28 CET, so this is bmo. The numbers are new (no trading update, no ad-hoc on results), the name is thin with two analysts and Q1 moved +10.75%, so abs_move_pct is 6.5, above the 3.7% history scale (which is biased low). The sign is close to a coin flip. H1 revenue and EBIT will be well up year on year because of the strong Q1, but management said on the Q1 call that the 20.9% Q1 EBIT margin is not a run-rate and that marketing and S/4HANA costs fall in Q2 and Q3, against a strong Q2 2025/26 comparison (EBIT EUR 4.9m on EUR 22.4m revenue, about a 22% margin). So p_up is 49 and the scaled number is about -0.1. The findings sum to +0.3 because the revenue-momentum and buyback findings slightly outweigh the margin finding. The two measurements differ in sign only at noise level, and the gap carries no information.

Management guidance, qualitative, reported by Montega from the Q1 call and the Hamburg investor days: headcount up about 10% to 550, R&D ratio towards about 33%, marketing campaign from September, S/4HANA costs mainly in Q2 and Q3, growth prioritised over EBIT
Share buyback 2026 II, up to EUR 5m (about 2.8% of share capital), running 5 Oct 2026 to 31 May 2027 at about 2,600 shares (about EUR 42k) a day
Prior-year H1 2025/26 comparison: revenue EUR 43.6m, EBIT EUR 7.3m, so Q2 2025/26 was revenue EUR 22.4m and EBIT EUR 4.9m

Q2 on its own: revenue up high single to low double digits, EBIT flat to down year on year because of the flagged cost step-up against a 22% Q2 2025/26 margin. Direction of the reaction: unknown.
Fabasoft gives no numeric guidance. Expect qualitative wording on investments and growth. A change is unlikely.
Unknown. Operating cash flow is seasonally weak in H1 (EUR 0.8m in H1 2025/26). Buyback and dividend outflows reduce cash.
Unknown. Possible comments on order intake, the public-sector pipeline (Bundes-ELAK with Mindbreeze AI) and headcount.

That is the 0.5% truncation floor, not a measured zero: anchor_covered is false, there is no positioning anchor, and priced_lean_pct (-0.14) is just the run-up. findings.finding: Management said on the Q1 call (reported by Montega) that the 20.9% Q1 EBIT margin is not a run-rate, and that marketing-campaign and S/4HANA costs fall mainly in Q2 and Q3. The Q2 2025/26 comparison was a strong EUR 4.9m EBIT on EUR 22.4m revenue (about 22%), so Q2 EBIT is likely flat to down year on year even though H1 EBIT will be up strongly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed history of how this name reacts to the quarter's margin. On Q1 (2026-08-13), when the margin beat, the stock rose about 10.75%. The baseline's earlier dates are cadence estimates and in some cases wrong (the Feb 2026 release was on 13 Feb, not 5 Feb), so they are not usable as a reaction history.
findings.original_quote: Der Vorstand betonte ausdrücklich die Priorisierung des Umsatzwachstums gegenüber dem EBIT, die in Q1 erreichte EBIT-Marge i.H.v. 20,9% gilt somit ausdrücklich nicht als Run-Rate ... Im weiteren Jahresverlauf ist zudem sowohl mit höheren Marketingkosten als auch Aufwendungen für die interne S/4HANA-Umstellung zu rechnen, die beide insbesondere in Q2 und Q3 anfallen dürften. (Translation: the board explicitly prioritised revenue growth over EBIT, so the 20.9% Q1 EBIT margin is explicitly not a run-rate; higher marketing costs and costs for the internal S/4HANA conversion are expected later in the year, falling mainly in Q2 and Q3.)
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: management told the market. What may not be priced is how hard the Q2 standalone comparison is. The Q2 2025/26 margin of about 22% is never printed on its own; it is H1 minus Q1, and the headline wire copy will show H1 up year on year. If this were fully priced, the stock would not have held about EUR 16.5 after the Q1 jump. If it were not priced at all, the lean would be clearly negative. It sits in between, so the finding is small.
findings.independence: The comparison figures come from the issuer's own H1 2025/26 and Q1 2025/26 releases (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/fabasoft-ag-fabasoft-increases-revenue-and-earnings-in-the-first-half-of-2025-2026/e8cd08e1-2cd9-40cc-9518-f8fbf5d59db4_en). The cost guidance has only the one source, Montega reporting the call (both Montega notes, 14 Aug and 2 Sep 2026).

findings.finding: Revenue momentum: recurring revenue rose 3.5% quarter on quarter to EUR 15.2m in Q1, professional-services utilisation was well above target in a surprisingly good order environment, and Montega expects double-digit FY 2026/27 growth. H1 revenue is therefore likely around +12-17% year on year, the first double-digit H1 in several years. Part of Q1 was a one-off: EUR 0.7m of licence revenue, equal to the whole of FY 2025/26.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026/27 at +19.7% revenue growth: stock +10.75% on the day. H1 2025/26 at +2.6% growth: the stock kept falling into January (Börse Express, 07.01.2026).
findings.original_quote: Durch das überraschend gute Auftragsumfeld bei einem gleichzeitig herausfordernden Rekrutierungsumfeld lag die Mitarbeiterzahl unter dem Niveau, das für den erzielten Umsatz als angemessen erachtet wird. Die Auslastungsquote im Professional Services-Geschäft lag somit deutlich oberhalb des Zielwerts. (Translation: because of the surprisingly good order environment and a difficult recruiting market, headcount was below the level considered appropriate for the revenue achieved, so professional-services utilisation was well above target.)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock rose from about EUR 13.3 (buyback fills, 20-24 Jul 2026) to about EUR 16.5 after Q1. It has been flat since (20-day run-up +2.8%), and Montega's target is EUR 27 at about 9.5x EV/EBIT. A Q2 that confirms double-digit growth is not fully in a stock that has stalled, but the one-off licence share argues against extrapolating Q1.
findings.independence: The issuer's Q1 release gives the recurring and total revenue figures directly (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/fabasoft-successfully-starts-the-new-fiscal-year/f57ba44f-85d7-478e-b065-c614ddc4afbe_en). The order-environment comment has only the one source.

findings.finding: The issuer's buyback (programme 2026 II, up to EUR 5m) has been buying about 2,600 shares (about EUR 42k) a day since 5 Oct 2026, roughly a quarter of the name's median turnover of $181k a day. It is a steady bid that keeps running through the results session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback ad-hocs (Dec 2025, Apr 2026, Sep 2026) are not tied to results days. No measured reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and weekly, so its existence is priced. What it adds on a thin name is a dampener on a downside gap, because the bank buys a fixed daily volume within safe-harbour volume limits. It does not move the mean much.
findings.independence: The 29 Sep 2026 ad-hoc that set up the programme: https://www.eqs-news.com/news/ad-hoc/fabasoft-ag-fabasoft-ag-resolves-share-buyback/410644fe-b7ae-4894-a9ed-d48dbb66fdcc_en

baseline_tension: There is little tension. The lean (-0.14) and the run-up (+2.8% over 20 days) are near zero, and the findings roughly offset (+0.3), so nothing here argues strongly against the price.
language_note: The German Montega notes (EQS/dpa-AFX Original-Research) carried what the call added to the release: the Q1 margin is explicitly not a run-rate, marketing and S/4HANA costs fall in Q2 and Q3, headcount goes up 10% to 550, and the order environment is surprisingly good. Fabasoft's English release says only 'we will focus our investments on strategically important future-oriented areas'.
The German press (Börse Express, 07.01.2026) recorded that the stock fell after the weak H1 2025/26 growth; the English sources carried only the release.
lessons_applied: Margin finding cut from -0.8 to -0.5: it lands inside what management already told the market (core table: inside guidance, toward 0).
Revenue-momentum finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6: part of Q1 was one-off licence revenue ('a beat made of a one-off is sold'), and the evidence is partly analyst inference.
Buyback finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2: already public and priced.

abs_move_pct raised from 6.0 to 6.5: the numbers are new (European base about 7.4%), the name is thin with two analysts, and 'too small about the move'. Held below 7 because no numeric guide exists to change (guide-unchanged median 2.3%).
